bridges.description: Support God's existence through the cumulative force of the selected arguments.
Connect cosmic origin, fine-tuning and morality to a personal good creator.
Use resurrection and defeater-sensitive experience to support Christian theism.
Support fallible disbelief by arguing that the evidence fits better without God.
Challenge divine explanation through natural reality, moral realism and suffering.
Challenge sectarian experience and historical inference as reliable routes to truth.

sections.title: Cosmic origin and causation
sections.rationale: The beginning of the universe, causal principle and nature of a first cause form a central route to the motion.

sections.title: Fine-tuning and design
sections.rationale: Life-permitting conditions and competing explanations form a distinct probabilistic route to design.

sections.title: Divine attributes and evil
sections.rationale: The coherence of a divine mind and the compatibility of perfect goodness with suffering bear directly on the proposed God.

sections.title: Objective morality
sections.rationale: The existence and grounding of objective moral requirements is a major independent line on both sides.

sections.title: Resurrection, experience and method
sections.rationale: Historical resurrection claims, religious experience and comparative evidential method distinguish Christian theism and test its warrant.

moves.inference: A cosmic beginning plus the causal premise implies a cause beyond spacetime.
